lines.en: Lina, look at that sky. It looks as if it is going to rain any minute and our picnic is ready.
lines.pt: Lina, olhe esse céu. Parece que vai chover a qualquer minuto, e nós temos o piquenique inteiro pronto.

lines.en: You are right. The clouds are so dark that it feels as though the day has already ended, Leo.
lines.pt: Você tem razão. As nuvens estão tão escuras que parece que o dia já acabou, Leo.

lines.en: And the wind is getting stronger. Our neighbour looks as if he is carrying his umbrella everywhere this week.
lines.pt: E o vento está ficando mais forte. Nosso vizinho parece que anda com o guarda-chuva para todo lado esta semana.

lines.en: Maybe he knows something we do not. He always talks as if he were a weather expert.
lines.pt: Talvez ele saiba algo que nós não sabemos. Ele sempre fala como se fosse um especialista em clima.

lines.en: True! Still, I would rather move the picnic indoors than sit in the park looking as though we had lost our minds.
lines.pt: Verdade! Mesmo assim, prefiro levar o piquenique para dentro a ficar no parque parecendo que perdemos a cabeça.

lines.en: Good idea. My living room is small, but it will be warm, and nobody has to pretend that the weather is fine.
lines.pt: Boa ideia. Minha sala é pequena, mas será aconchegante, e ninguém precisa fingir que o tempo está bom.

lines.en: Wait, did you just feel a drop? It sounds as if the rain has started on the roof of the cafe.
lines.pt: Espere, você sentiu uma gota? Parece que a chuva começou no telhado do café ali adiante.

lines.en: Yes! Let us hurry before everything gets wet. You look as though you are about to run a race.
lines.pt: Sim! Vamos depressa antes que tudo molhe. Você parece que está prestes a correr uma maratona, aliás.

lines.en: I am only protecting the sandwiches! Last month I trusted the forecast, and we ended up eating cold pasta in the car.
lines.pt: Só estou protegendo os sanduíches! No mês passado confiei na previsão e acabamos comendo macarrão frio no carro.

lines.en: I remember. You complained as if it were my fault.
lines.pt: Eu me lembro. Você reclamou como se fosse culpa minha, embora você mesma tivesse escolhido o parque.

lines.en: Fair enough. Come on, the first drops are falling, and I want the best seat next to the window at your place.
lines.pt: Justo. Vamos, as primeiras gotas estão caindo e eu quero o melhor lugar perto da janela na sua casa.

work.title: Chuva Repentina sobre a Ponte Shin-Ohashi
work.note: Gravura em madeira de Utagawa Hiroshige, da série Cem Vistas Famosas de Edo, que mostra pessoas atravessando uma ponte sobre o rio, com guarda-chuvas e chapéus, sob nuvens escuras e chuva forte. facts.label: Aparências e impressões
facts.sub: It looks as if…, as though…, as if he were…, as if nothing had happened.

facts.label: as if + presente
facts.sub: Use as if ou as though + presente para uma impressão provável: It looks as if it is going to rain. Em português: “parece que vai chover”.

facts.label: as if + were
facts.sub: Use as if + passado para algo irreal: He talks as if he were an expert. Para be, usamos were: as if I were rich. A pessoa não é especialista de verdade.

compare.ask: It looks as if it is going to rain.
compare.br: No Brasil, dizemos “parece que vai chover” e “ele fala como se soubesse tudo”.
compare.tip: Diga: “It looks as if it is going to rain.”
compare.us: Em inglês: It looks as if it is going to rain; He talks as if he knew everything. Use presente para o provável e passado para o irreal.

solo: Peça uma experiência pessoal do aluno com essa diferença.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: It looks as if it is going to rain means rain is likely.
As if and as though have very different meanings.
He talks as if he were an expert describes something unreal.
items.why: Yes, he is not an expert.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: It looks as if it is going to rain means rain is likely. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
As if and as though have very different meanings. → Falso (They mean almost the same.)
He talks as if he were an expert describes something unreal. → Verdadeiro (Yes, he is not an expert.)

pages.title: A picnic and a dark sky · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a grey afternoon in Austin. Dana carries a basket full of food. Nina brings a blanket and two cold drinks. They walk towards their favourite park. The sky changes colour very quickly. Both friends stop and look up.

“Nina, look at that sky. It looks as if it is going to rain any minute and our picnic is ready.” says Dana. “You are right. The clouds are so dark that it feels as though the day has already ended, Dana.” says Nina. “And the wind is getting stronger. Our neighbour looks as if he is carrying his umbrella everywhere this week.” says Dana.
